tasks.short: Answer hardware and software questions, confirm the answer helped, and record the outcome.

steps.what: Read the inquiry and ask for missing device, software or error details.
Register the inquiry, category and responsible queue in the {HELPDESK}.
Find the relevant approved instructions in {DOCS}.
Explain the instructions and send the answer to the user.

loop.input: Clarified inquiry and selected approved instructions for the supported version.
loop.output: A short answer with ordered instructions and links to the approved source.
loop.check: Check every procedural step against the source; the specialist approves before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; escalate to diagnosis if the source does not answer the question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover common answers, but varied questions need plain-language adaptation to the user's context.

steps.what: Talk through unclear instructions and confirm whether the answer resolved the inquiry.
Record the outcome and close or escalate the inquiry in the {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake, routing and outcome capture in {HELPDESK}, with version-filtered access to approved instructions in {DOCS}. Serve unchanged approved instructions directly through self-service; use a bounded model loop for tailored replies, approved by the specialist before sending through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. Unresolved inquiries become linked incidents for diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated answers were scattered across messages and documents, while instructions often lacked clear device or version labels.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured intake and searchable approved instructions address much of the task. A small drafting loop can adapt the remaining answers without controlling the user's device.
tasks.still_hard: Users may describe symptoms rather than the underlying question. Incorrect guidance, accessibility barriers and stale instructions still need human attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise confusion or anxiety, explain at the user's pace and notice when a simple question needs investigation.

ambition.what: After-hours self-service for approved, low-risk hardware and software instructions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time registering inquiries and searching for repeated answers, and more time helping users who remain stuck. They can gain delegated authority to prioritise knowledge gaps for review; publishing new guidance still follows the existing approval route.

reach.task: Prepare clear written replies from approved information.
reach.learn: Use plain language, source checks and a clear next action.

reach.task: Recognise when an inquiry needs specialist escalation.
reach.learn: Use brief clarification questions and record the user's attempted steps.

evidence.claim: Configured forms, routing and filtered knowledge search can reduce routine inquiry handling without a model.
TOPdesk documents category suggestions and reviewed knowledge drafting; tailored reply drafting here is a proposed extension.
Microsoft reports fewer IT tickets from employee self-service at a much larger organisation; the case gives no transferable savings forecast.
If a user-facing AI chatbot is introduced, applicable AI interaction disclosure requirements must be addressed.

assumptions: This task covers known-use questions; uncertain faults pass into the separate diagnosis task.
Unchanged approved instructions use deterministic self-service; tailored model replies require review.
Structured intake reduces missing information, but phone and walk-up support remain available.
Automated closure requires explicit resolution confirmation; silence alone does not count.
GDPR applies to inquiry data, and national rules govern any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Actual inquiry volumes by channel, language and topic.
Coverage, ownership and version accuracy of approved instructions.
Whether users can access an authenticated self-service channel.
Permitted handling of screenshots, personal data and confidential inquiries.
Existing closure, escalation and publication approval rules.
research_questions: Which inquiry topics have sufficiently stable instructions for unattended self-service?
How often does filtered search return instructions for the wrong software version?
Can users complete the proposed instructions without additional explanation?
new_work: Review tailored replies before sending.
Maintain instruction labels, versions and ownership.
Inspect failed searches and unresolved self-service sessions.
Route unsupported questions to diagnosis.
Test guidance with users who have different language and accessibility needs.
tasks.statement: Answer user inquiries regarding computer software or hardware operation to resolve problems.

tasks.short: Run operational checks, inspect results, and identify computer faults.

steps.what: Choose checks and expected outcomes from the support instructions.
Enter diagnostic commands in the {OTHER} device console and observe operation.
Compare diagnostic output with expected operation.
Interpret unexpected results and decide whether further diagnosis is needed.
Attach results to the service ticket and route any escalation.

tasks.design: Build a small library of read-only diagnostic scripts on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, using approved access to the {OTHER} endpoint administration system. Deterministic assertions return pass, fail, or unknown and attach evidence to the {HELPDESK}. The specialist selects the checks and investigates unexpected results; no model or autonomous agent is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks differ across devices, expected results are often poorly documented, and console output requires manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing command interfaces support repeatable checks. AI-assisted coding can help turn known procedures into scripts and assertions, subject to ordinary engineering verification.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults and incomplete expected outcomes resist fixed assertions. A passing technical check may still miss a user's actual problem.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses useful tests, recognises misleading results, and connects technical evidence to the reported symptom.

ambition.what: Readiness checks before standard endpoint rollouts

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from watching commands run to investigating failed and unknown checks. With explicit delegation, the specialist can pause a standard rollout when agreed readiness criteria fail.

reach.task: Run a guided user-facing smoke test after a technical fix.
reach.learn: Learn observable acceptance criteria, clear instructions, and escalation triggers.

evidence.claim: Allowlisted diagnostic commands and deterministic assertions can automate known operational checks.
GitHub Copilot supports coding assistance, but this does not demonstrate reliable endpoint diagnosis.
Developer productivity evidence varies: METR's early study found slower completion and its later rerun was inconclusive.

assumptions: The baseline concerns routine operational verification, with advanced diagnosis handled as an exception.
Console work is screen-heavy; the supplied in-person share is a weak fit for this specific task.
Automated commands are read-only and exclude disruptive load tests or configuration changes.
Missing output, unsupported versions, and timeouts produce unknown, never pass.
The installation task covers physical and user acceptance checks; this task covers command-based verification.
Remaining percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which checks are repeated most often, and are expected outcomes documented?
Which devices expose approved diagnostic access?
Which tests may affect service availability?
Can specialists receive delegated rollout-pause authority?
Does diagnostic collection require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: How often do automated pass results disagree with observed user problems?
Can supported device variants share assertions without hiding important differences?
new_work: Maintain commands, expected outcomes, version compatibility, and timeouts.
Investigate unknown results and false passes.
Review diagnostic access and remove unnecessary personal data from captured output.
tasks.statement: Enter commands and observe system functioning to verify correct operations and detect errors.

tasks.short: Install software and equipment, make minor repairs, and confirm that users can work.

steps.what: Read the service ticket, asset record, and installation specifications.
Inspect equipment and ask the user to demonstrate the fault.
Choose a repair or installation method within delegated authority.
Connect equipment, replace minor components, and make physical adjustments.
Install approved software through the {OTHER} endpoint administration console.
Check equipment operation and confirm the user's normal activity works.
Update the service ticket and asset record.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to show asset details, approved instructions from the {DOCS}, and an installation checklist. Use the {OTHER} endpoint administration system for approved package deployment after the support specialist confirms the target and package; return deployment results to the {HELPDESK}. Physical work and user acceptance stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical variation limits automation. Package preparation, device enrolment, and disconnected asset records also make standard deployments costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing deployment controls and structured checklists cover routine cases. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting deployment results to records, without changing the physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, unsupported equipment, missing parts, and installations needing elevated access remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist notices physical clues, chooses a proportionate repair, and checks whether the user can actually work.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer installation clicks and record updates, but still includes site visits and repairs. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Guide users through basic equipment checks before booking a visit.
reach.learn: Learn clear troubleshooting questions, accessibility needs, and when to stop and escalate.

evidence.claim: Managed package deployment and structured asset updates can reduce routine installation work; physical repairs remain manual.
GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review, which can help build adapters; this does not establish a delivery speed multiplier.

assumptions: The baseline is internal user support in a mid-size European company with a {HELPDESK}.
Shares represent a mixed workload; hardware-only and software-only cases skip different steps.
Standard software packages and enrolled devices are available for the proposed deployment path.
Remaining percentages and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: Which devices are enrolled and which deployment controls are licensed?
Which installations require additional approval or customer permission?
How often do physical repairs, package exceptions, and user visits occur?
What access and consultation are required under national rules?
research_questions: Can deployment results update asset records without duplicating or overwriting technician observations?
Which common packages have reliable detection, rollback, and restart handling?
new_work: Maintain approved packages, compatibility rules, and rollback instructions.
Review deployment targets and handle failed installations.
Check that automatic record updates match completed work.
tasks.statement: Install and perform minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications.

tasks.short: Check daily system health, confirm user impact, and escalate performance problems.

steps.what: Inspect endpoint and infrastructure monitoring screens for slowdowns, failures and capacity warnings.
Compare health exceptions with open incidents in the {HELPDESK}.
Ask affected users how the slowdown or failure disrupts their work.
Set incident priority and assign investigation or escalation in the {HELPDESK}.
Copy health figures and incident status into a daily email.

tasks.design: Configure health views in endpoint and infrastructure monitoring tools in {OTHER}; use a small integration on {DATA_PLATFORM} to link exceptions to {HELPDESK} incidents by device, service and time. A shared {BI} view replaces the copied daily email, while people confirm business impact and set escalation priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Monitoring existed, but inconsistent device identifiers and separate incident records made reconciliation and reporting manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitoring configuration and small API adapters can cover collection and matching. AI coding may shorten adapter development; no new model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, incomplete telemetry and competing business priorities still require investigation. New staff monitoring requires a proportionate purpose and consultation under applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand which apparently small failure blocks important work, and negotiate the right response across teams.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of emerging capacity risks before users report a failure.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking screens and copying figures toward investigating meaningful exceptions. The specialist can gain delegated authority to reprioritise investigations; infrastructure changes still follow existing approval rights.

reach.task: Adjust queue coverage when service failures increase demand.
reach.learn: Translate service impact and incident arrival patterns into staffing needs.

evidence.claim: Configured monitoring, threshold rules and identifier matching can automate routine health collection without a model.
Security logging requires a necessary and proportionate purpose; this does not justify unrestricted employee observation.
Dutch works council consent can apply to employee monitoring arrangements; other countries require checking national rules.

assumptions: Monitoring already covers the main managed devices and services.
Structured telemetry outweighs the supplied prior's high meeting share for routine collection; impact assessment remains human.
Build estimates cover one initial service group and working days of effort, not statutory waiting periods.
unknowns: Telemetry coverage, retention and API access.
Whether device and service identifiers match across tools.
Who uses the daily email and whether the shared view meets their needs.
Country, employee representation and whether the proposed telemetry changes require consultation.
research_questions: Which health signals detect user-visible degradation with the fewest false alarms?
Which supported interfaces provide service health without collecting user content?
new_work: Tune alert thresholds and suppression windows.
Resolve unmatched device and service identifiers.
Review false alarms and missed incidents.
Maintain access controls, retention settings and integration credentials.
tasks.statement: Oversee the daily performance of computer systems.

tasks.short: Prepare employee equipment, install approved software, and confirm the setup works.

steps.what: Read the equipment request, employee details and required start date in the {HELPDESK}.
Select available equipment and an approved software profile in the {HELPDESK}.
Unpack equipment, position peripherals and connect power, network and display cables.
Install the operating system and approved software through endpoint management in {OTHER}.
Test login, connectivity, applications and peripherals on the equipment.
Hand over equipment and confirm the employee can use the required tools.
Update asset assignment, installation status and request completion in the {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: Configure equipment requests and approved setup profiles in {HELPDESK}, with permitted employee details supplied from {HCM}. Endpoint management in {OTHER} deploys the selected profile and returns installation results; a small integration updates asset records after recorded employee acceptance. People connect hardware, check physical operation and handle individual needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setup profiles, stock records and employee requests were maintained separately. Packaging reliable software deployments and handling unusual peripherals took effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Mature endpoint provisioning and request workflows already handle standard setups. Small adapters can connect their records without adding a model.
tasks.still_hard: Cabling, faulty hardware, unusual software and accessibility needs remain hands-on. Licensing and nonstandard access need existing approval routes.
tasks.human_edge: Notice practical barriers at the desk and help the employee become comfortable using the equipment.

ambition.what: A pre-start accessibility setup clinic for employees requesting adapted equipment.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time clicking through standard installations and updating records. Saved time supports physical checks and individual setup sessions; purchasing and access approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Guide a new user through first use of an unfamiliar service.
reach.learn: Use plain-language demonstrations and ask the user to show successful completion.

evidence.claim: Standard endpoint profiles can automate operating-system and application deployment while physical installation remains manual.
Request workflows and installation callbacks can maintain asset and completion records without a model.
AI coding speed gains vary by context, so build estimates should not assume a universal acceleration.

assumptions: Most devices belong to a managed estate with approved deployment profiles.
Standard software and access entitlements are authorised before deployment.
The setup task covers new employees and equipment replacements.
Consultation effort applies if employee data use or monitoring changes; national rules determine the requirement.
unknowns: How many devices already support unattended provisioning.
Whether asset records are accurate and available through an interface.
Software packaging, licence availability and supported hardware diversity.
Who approves nonstandard equipment and accessibility requests.
Employee data access and applicable consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which setup checks can the existing endpoint tools perform reliably without user credentials?
Which peripherals and application packages need a physical pilot before rollout?
new_work: Maintain deployment profiles and software packages.
Handle failed installations and stock mismatches.
Check that automated completion waits for employee acceptance.
Keep accessibility requests restricted to people who need the details.
tasks.statement: Set up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software.

tasks.short: Record support activity, technical problems, installation work, and remedial actions.

steps.what: Retrieve activity and diagnostic records from the {OTHER} endpoint administration system.
Enter dates, devices, problem codes, and actions into the service ticket.
Write a short account of the problem and remedial action.

loop.input: Ticket history, structured actions, technician notes, and recorded user acceptance.
loop.output: A concise resolution note with links to supporting evidence and explicit missing details.
loop.check: Validate references and required fields; the specialist checks accuracy and removes unnecessary personal data.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per ticket; unresolved contradictions return to the specialist for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields cover standard actions, but varied technician notes need language interpretation for a useful narrative.

steps.what: Update asset details to reflect completed installation or repair.
Check completeness, correct discrepancies, and finalise the activity record.
Copy completed activity into a separate daily handover document.

tasks.design: Connect timestamped events from the {OTHER} endpoint administration system to structured records in the {HELPDESK}, with stable event identifiers and correction history. A bounded model loop drafts resolution notes for review, while configured validation flags missing evidence. Replace the copied daily document with a saved {HELPDESK} handover view.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technicians bridge disconnected activity logs, tickets, and asset records by hand. Free-text explanations do not fit simple field mappings.
tasks.enabler_now: Event interfaces and configured forms handle structured capture. Reviewed drafting can turn technician notes into concise narratives without inventing actions.
tasks.still_hard: Off-system repairs leave incomplete evidence. Incorrect device matching and copied sensitive data can make automatic records misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes what was observed, what was attempted, and what actually resolved the user's problem.
tasks.altitude: Less transcription leaves time to investigate recurring faults and propose prevention work. The specialist gains a stronger basis for recommending fixes; change approval remains with the service owner.

reach.task: Prepare reusable user instructions from reviewed resolution notes.
reach.learn: Learn technical accuracy checks, audience-appropriate wording, and personal-data removal.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk supports ticket summaries and drafts knowledge items for review, supporting the reviewed narrative component.
Deterministic event linking, required fields, and saved handover views can remove duplicate recordkeeping.
Microsoft reports fewer IT tickets after employee self-service adoption; its much larger setting does not establish savings for this recordkeeping design.
GDPR requires appropriate handling of personal data. Employee consultation depends on national rules; EU AI Act duties depend on the actual use.

assumptions: The {HELPDESK} is the primary support record; a separate handover document is an illustrative duplication pattern.
Automatic asset updates record observed facts and do not grant access or change entitlements.
Installation record updates described in the first task use this same capability; savings are not additive.
Activity capture supports service records and excludes staff performance scoring.
The consultation and access range includes employee representation where national rules require it.
Remaining percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Is activity duplicated in handover documents or maintained only in the {HELPDESK}?
Are event identifiers and device identifiers stable across systems?
Which actions happen without machine-readable evidence?
What retention, access, employee consultation, and model-processing arrangements are approved?
Who owns corrections when source logs and technician accounts disagree?
research_questions: How accurately can events be linked to tickets without relying on free-text guesses?
Which record fields improve fault prevention rather than merely add administrative detail?
new_work: Review resolution drafts and resolve contradictory evidence.
Maintain event mappings, retention rules, and access permissions.
Monitor duplicate events and incorrect asset matches.
Prepare and validate the recurring-fault prevention brief.
tasks.statement: Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.

tasks.short: Investigate computer problems, choose a safe remedy, and verify recovery with the user.

steps.what: Ask the user about symptoms, recent changes and the effect on their work.
Inspect device diagnostics and relevant logs through remote-support tools in {OTHER}.
Read relevant technical manuals and known fixes in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Relevant approved manual passages, known fixes, device version and diagnostic results.
loop.output: Remedy candidates with source passages, prerequisites and uncertainties.
loop.check: Require retrievable citations and matching versions; the specialist checks applicability before choosing a remedy.
loop.stop: One retrieval and extraction pass, then one correction pass; return no recommendation if evidence remains insufficient.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search retrieves documents, but useful prerequisites and exceptions occur in varied technical prose.

steps.what: Choose a remedy, check permissions and agree any disruption with the user.
Apply the authorised remedy through remote-support tools in {OTHER}.
Ask the user to repeat the affected activity and confirm recovery.
Record the investigation, remedy and outcome in the {HELPDESK}.

loop.input: Recorded diagnostic results, executed actions and explicit user recovery confirmation.
loop.output: A draft resolution record distinguishing observations, actions and unresolved symptoms.
loop.check: Check actions against execution logs, remove secrets and require specialist approval before saving.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; use a structured manual record if evidence is incomplete.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured logs capture actions, but the user's outcome and investigation reasoning remain free text.

tasks.design: Link {HELPDESK} incidents to allowlisted, read-only diagnostics from remote-support tools in {OTHER}, and retrieve approved guidance from {DOCS}. Bounded model loops extract cited remedy candidates and draft resolution records; the specialist authorises the remedy before any configured repair action runs. User conversations and recovery confirmation remain part of the service.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnostics, manuals and incident notes were separate, and reliable guidance depended on knowing the exact device and software version.
tasks.enabler_now: Diagnostic APIs and indexed documentation can supply a controlled evidence set. Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce reading and paperwork without autonomous troubleshooting.
tasks.still_hard: Novel faults, misleading logs and interacting changes resist fixed procedures. Remote access and diagnostic collection must respect GDPR, user permissions and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a plausible explanation from a safe remedy, manage disruption and recognise when specialist escalation is needed.

ambition.what: A recurring-fault review that turns repeated incidents into a tested prevention proposal.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week testing hypotheses and helping users recover, with less evidence gathering and note writing. They can gain authority to propose prevention work from incident patterns; approval for disruptive changes stays with the designated change owner.

reach.task: Coach staff on diagnosis quality using resolved incidents.
reach.learn: Separate evidence, hypotheses and confirmed causes when reviewing a case.

evidence.claim: Allowlisted diagnostics and approved repair scripts can use deterministic execution while people handle exceptions.
TOPdesk documents ticket summarisation and reviewed knowledge drafting; this supports the paperwork component, not autonomous diagnosis.
Cited extraction from version-matched manuals is a proposed bounded workflow, not a documented outcome in this digest.

assumptions: Diagnostics collect a fixed minimum evidence set and cannot execute repairs.
The specialist's remedy approval covers only their delegated rights; restricted changes require the existing change owner.
Existing configured repair actions cover some routine fixes; novel repairs remain manual.
Call recording is not required: the design can use specialist-entered notes.
unknowns: Approved remote-access methods and diagnostic permissions.
Availability and currency of technical manuals and known fixes.
Which repairs specialists may authorise and which require another approver.
Sensitive information present in logs and incident histories.
National consultation requirements for changed remote-support or logging practices.
research_questions: How reliably can extracted guidance distinguish supported versions and prerequisites?
Which diagnostic bundles provide enough evidence without collecting unnecessary user data?
Which repeated remedies are safe to package with explicit recovery checks?
new_work: Review cited recommendations and resolution drafts.
Maintain diagnostic allowlists and repair packages.
Retire obsolete manuals and known fixes.
Investigate unsupported suggestions and failed recovery checks.
Audit access and remove sensitive material from diagnostic records.
tasks.statement: Read technical manuals, confer with users, or conduct computer diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems or to provide technical assistance and support.

tasks.short: Discuss user needs and agree requirements for new systems or changes.

steps.what: Read the change request and gather related support records.
Arrange a discussion with users and the service owner.
Discuss workarounds, needs, constraints, and conflicting priorities.
Write requirements, acceptance criteria, and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Facilitator notes, linked support records, and a requirements template.
loop.output: Requirements draft with source references, proposed acceptance criteria, and explicit open questions.
loop.check: Check required sections and source references automatically; the specialist checks meaning and unsupported commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per workshop; missing evidence remains an open question, then use manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the document but cannot reliably turn varied discussion notes into clear requirements.

steps.what: Resolve trade-offs and approve the requirements baseline with user representatives.

tasks.design: Pull linked records from the {HELPDESK}, {PROJECT}, and {DOCS} into a requirements brief, and configure scheduling through the {CALENDAR}. A bounded model loop converts facilitator notes into a sourced requirements draft in the {DOCS}. The specialist reviews the draft, while the service owner approves scope and trade-offs.
tasks.previous_blocker: The conversation contains tacit needs and competing interests. Manual preparation and document writing were bundled with that human work.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked records and templates make preparation repeatable. A bounded drafting loop can organise notes while leaving uncertainty visible.
tasks.still_hard: Users may disagree, omit important constraints, or describe a preferred solution rather than the underlying need.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist earns trust, notices unstated constraints, and helps people negotiate a workable compromise.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and drafting can make room for clinics with evening-shift users. The specialist can recommend priorities with better evidence; scope and budget approval remain with the service owner.

reach.task: Translate recurring staff problems into prioritised service change requests.
reach.learn: Learn demand analysis, acceptance criteria, and how to distinguish urgency from business impact.

evidence.claim: Linked record retrieval and template-based requirements preparation are feasible without autonomous agents.
Drafting requirements from workshop notes is a proposed bounded application, not a documented case in this digest.
TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review, demonstrating adjacent reviewed drafting rather than requirements approval.

assumptions: The specialist facilitates requirements discussions; a service owner approves the baseline.
Facilitator notes are used without requiring meeting recordings.
Invitations use an agreed participant list and permitted internal scheduling rules.
The conversation remains the largest step, consistent with the supplied priors.
Remaining percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Who may approve scope, budget, accessibility requirements, and acceptance criteria?
Can support records be linked to change requests reliably?
Which user groups currently miss requirements discussions?
Which data may be included in model inputs, and what consultation do national rules require?
research_questions: Can reviewers distinguish sourced requirements from proposed acceptance criteria consistently?
Does structured preparation reveal missing user groups before workshops?
new_work: Review drafts for invented commitments and missing dissent.
Maintain templates and source links.
Follow up open questions and arrange clinics for underserved users.
tasks.statement: Confer with staff, users, and management to establish requirements for new systems or modifications.

tasks.short: Create practical technology guidance and teach users how to work with hardware and software.

steps.what: Review recurring support topics and existing guidance to identify training needs.
Confirm learners' tasks, starting knowledge and accessibility needs.
Draft instructions, screenshots, practice exercises and session materials.

loop.input: Approved procedures, sanitised screenshots and a defined learner task.
loop.output: A lesson, quick guide and practice exercise using a fixed template.
loop.check: Check source coverage, version labels and personal-data removal; test instructions in the target interface.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per lesson; unsupported instructions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting technical prose to learner knowledge needs language judgement; layout uses templates.

steps.what: Test the instructions and approve accurate, accessible learning materials.
Publish materials, arrange sessions and invite the intended learners.
Demonstrate tasks, observe practice and help learners overcome difficulties.
Record participation and send follow-up exercises and a feedback request.

tasks.design: Configure topic counts from the {HELPDESK} and reusable lesson templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares guidance from approved procedures; a specialist tests and approves it before the {LMS} publishes it and the {CALENDAR} schedules sessions. Configured follow-ups record participation and collect feedback while practical coaching stays human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing each guide and coordinating sessions took time. Existing material often lacked a clear version, owner or review date.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and configured learning workflows already handle publication and follow-up. Bounded drafting reduces adaptation work without claiming to understand each learner.
tasks.still_hard: Screenshots and instructions age quickly, and accessibility requires real testing. GDPR applies to learning records; national rules may require consultation when tracking changes.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing confusion, building confidence and changing the explanation while someone practises.

ambition.what: Short accessible onboarding lessons for shift workers who miss daytime sessions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week coaching and testing whether guidance works. They can prioritise lesson topics within an agreed curriculum remit; employee performance decisions remain outside this task.

reach.task: Teach a user a repeatable self-service procedure.
reach.learn: Plain-language explanations, teach-back and recognition of accessibility barriers.

evidence.claim: Reviewed knowledge-item drafting is available today; this supports guidance preparation but does not establish teaching effectiveness.
A large internal self-service deployment reports fewer support tickets; its scale and baseline limit transfer to this company size.
Learning publication, enrolment and follow-up can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and delivery ranges are planning estimates.
Topic counts use existing categories and aggregate demand rather than employee rankings.
The OTHER slot means the hardware or software interface being taught.
The audience is internal, so publication and invitations are internal writes.
Build scope covers one lesson family and existing learning software.
Access work includes GDPR review and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Which guidance is authoritative and who approves changes?
Which languages, accessibility needs and shifts must be covered?
Can the learning system publish materials and record attendance through configuration?
What participation data may be retained, and for how long?
Who may set curriculum priorities?
research_questions: Which recurring questions would benefit from training rather than a software fix?
Can learners complete the target task after using the guide?
Which interface changes should trigger a material review?
new_work: Test generated instructions and practice exercises.
Maintain source procedures, screenshots and review dates.
Check accessibility and learner comprehension.
Handle unanswered learner questions and update approved guidance.
Maintain enrolment rules and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Develop training materials and procedures, or train users in the proper use of hardware or software.

tasks.short: Refer major faults to service providers and coordinate their resolution.

steps.what: Check the incident history, device record and service entitlement.
Decide whether specialist service is needed and select the escalation route.
Assemble fault details, attempted fixes and relevant diagnostic attachments.

loop.input: Selected incident notes and diagnostic excerpts, with secrets removed.
loop.output: Source-linked fault summary and attempted fixes in a fixed request template.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; specialist checks accuracy and disclosure.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing evidence returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Chronological free-text notes need summarising; entitlement fields remain deterministic.

steps.what: Review disclosure and submit the service request through the provider's channel.
Agree service arrangements, clarify findings and resolve responsibility disputes.
Record the service reference, agreed plan and next follow-up date.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to join incident, asset and entitlement records and generate a service-request template. A bounded model drafts the fault narrative; the specialist approves disclosure before submission through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. Structured service references and agreed dates feed the {HELPDESK}, with reminders in the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Entitlements, diagnostic notes and provider channels were disconnected. Disputed responsibility still required a person.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing service workflows cover routing and reminders. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of missing connectors; bounded summarisation handles incident prose.
tasks.still_hard: Provider interfaces vary, and warranty disputes need judgement. GDPR requires controlled disclosure; paid work still follows purchasing authority.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparent device fault is a wider incident, and negotiating a workable service plan.

ambition.what: A weekly recurring-fault review proposing replacement or supplier action.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer evidence hunts and more stalled-case resolution. The specialist can prioritise recurring-fault investigations within the support remit; purchasing rights do not change.

reach.task: Coordinate updates during a prolonged service interruption.
reach.learn: Expectation setting, clear next-update commitments and complaint recovery.

evidence.claim: Ticket summarisation is available today; this supports request preparation, not autonomous service commitments.
Structured entitlement checks, routing and follow-up reminders can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The service desk has linked asset records and reusable escalation rules.
Submission covers an existing entitlement; new expenditure follows a separate approval.
Build ranges assume one service desk and one provider connection, including access review and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which provider channels support submission and status exchange?
Where are current entitlements and service references stored?
Who may approve diagnostic disclosure and chargeable work?
Does employee consultation apply to the proposed logging changes?
research_questions: Which required request fields can be populated through existing configuration?
What information can be excluded from diagnostic attachments without weakening fault assessment?
new_work: Review generated fault summaries and attachments.
Resolve unmatched entitlements and failed provider submissions.
Maintain routing rules, connector credentials and request templates.
Enter agreed service dates when conversations produce no structured record.
tasks.statement: Refer major hardware or software problems or defective products to vendors or technicians for service.

tasks.short: Evaluate hardware or software and recommend improvements or upgrades.

steps.what: Clarify user problems, constraints and evaluation criteria with stakeholders.
Gather specifications, support history, lifecycle dates and cost information.

loop.input: Selected specifications, quotes and lifecycle documents.
loop.output: A comparison table with source passages, dates, units and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types and units; verify consequential claims against cited passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document; unresolved fields remain unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents use inconsistent prose and layouts; structured records use direct mappings.

steps.what: Run representative compatibility, performance and usability tests with selected users.
Compare options against criteria and assess operational trade-offs.
Write the evaluation, recommendation and proposed upgrade sequence.

loop.input: Approved comparison data and the specialist's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: A report explaining evidence, trade-offs, uncertainties and upgrade sequence.
loop.check: Recalculate costs in code; check every factual claim against supplied evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are removed or marked unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining mixed technical and user evidence needs prose; calculations and tables remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss trade-offs and obtain a decision on the recommendation.
Record the decision, rationale and follow-up evaluation date.

tasks.design: Use a reusable evaluation brief and cost model in the {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET}, with evidence drawn from the {HELPDESK} and {PROCUREMENT}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare comparisons and reports; the specialist runs tests and chooses the recommendation. The IT manager's decision creates a record and follow-up in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence collection and report preparation were repetitive, while evaluation criteria and test conditions changed between requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and calculation templates reduce setup. Bounded extraction handles document variation, and AI-assisted coding can make small evidence connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Representative trials, accessibility needs and migration risks remain context dependent. Staff usage data requires GDPR safeguards and any consultation required by national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing realistic tests and recognising when a technically stronger option would make users' work harder.

ambition.what: A quarterly evidence-based refresh shortlist for ageing equipment.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into collecting specifications and formatting reports; more goes into trials and migration advice. The specialist can initiate shortlist reviews within an agreed remit; budget approval remains with the IT manager.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Assess how an upgrade changes administrative workflows.
reach.learn: Task observation, service continuity and the cost of retraining.

evidence.claim: Prompted document metadata extraction exists, but its outputs can be wrong and require validation.
Comparison templates, cost calculations and repeatable test scripts can reduce evaluation preparation.
Developer field trials document productivity gains; they do not establish a 10-to-100-fold build improvement here.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates requiring a local pilot.
The OTHER slot in testing means device diagnostics and software test utilities.
Quotes, specifications and incident history can be accessed lawfully.
Build scope covers one evaluation template and limited connectors, not a laboratory or procurement replacement.
Consent and access estimates include any consultation required under national rules; elapsed time may be longer.
unknowns: Which evaluation criteria and cost assumptions are already approved?
Are representative test devices, environments and users available?
Who can authorise trials and shortlist reviews?
Will the evaluation collect individual employee usage data?
research_questions: Which comparison fields can be obtained as structured exports?
Which tests predict actual user outcomes rather than benchmark scores?
How reliably do source-linked extractions preserve exclusions and lifecycle conditions?
new_work: Verify extracted specifications, exclusions and lifecycle dates.
Maintain cost assumptions and comparison templates.
Keep test environments representative.
Review whether prior recommendations achieved their expected outcomes.
tasks.statement: Prepare evaluations of software or hardware, and recommend improvements or upgrades.

tasks.short: Keep technical knowledge current through reading, seminars and practical evaluation.

steps.what: Review recurring incidents and identify knowledge gaps.
Find relevant manuals, technical articles and upcoming seminars.
Read selected material and work through technical examples.
Attend seminars and question presenters about practical problems.
Judge which techniques suit the supported environment.
Write and share useful learning with the support team.

loop.input: Selected notes, source references and the specialist's applicability decisions.
loop.output: A short learning brief with source references and proposed support improvements.
loop.check: Require a source for each technical claim; the specialist checks accuracy before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing evidence returns the brief to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies headings but cannot condense varied prose into a useful explanation.

tasks.design: Configure topic subscriptions and saved searches in {DOCS}, informed by recurring incidents in {HELPDESK}. A bounded drafting loop turns selected notes into a cited learning brief for review before sharing through {CHAT}; reading, questioning and practical evaluation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources are scattered, and deciding what deserves attention requires knowledge of the supported environment. Collecting material was easier to automate than learning from it.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured subscriptions handle collection, while a small drafting loop reduces the effort of sharing lessons. AI-assisted coding can help connect incident categories to source filters, without assuming a particular speed gain.
tasks.still_hard: Deep understanding, useful questions and testing whether advice fits local configurations still take time. Source subscriptions may require licences.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises misleading advice, connects new knowledge to past incidents and learns through practice.

ambition.what: Monthly troubleshooting clinic for reception staff.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding material and writing summaries; more goes into practice and teaching. The specialist can choose clinic topics within an agreed remit, with no added production-change authority.

reach.task: Resolve common workstation and meeting-room problems before escalating.
reach.learn: Observe reception workflows and learn how to teach short, accessible troubleshooting routines.

evidence.claim: Configured source filters and incident reports can reduce collection work; learning itself still requires practice.
TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for human review, supporting the feasibility of reviewed knowledge drafting.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative estimates for a learning cycle, not measured customer time.
Approved technical sources provide searchable content or subscriptions.
Build ranges cover a small source collection and one support team.
Collection is automated only within selected topics; the specialist still chooses what to study.
No employee-level learning or productivity scoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which source subscriptions and content licences are available?
Are incident categories reliable enough to inform learning priorities?
Can the specialist reserve time for practice and a reception clinic?
What access and consultation are required for the proposed data use?
research_questions: How accurately do topic filters identify useful material for the supported hardware and software versions?
new_work: Maintain source lists and topic filters.
Check draft briefs against original sources.
Remove obsolete guidance and handle conflicting advice.
Keep incident examples free of unnecessary personal data.
tasks.statement: Read trade magazines and technical manuals, or attend conferences and seminars to maintain knowledge of hardware and software.

tasks.short: Check ordered equipment, test readiness and prepare it for user delivery.

steps.what: Read the approved order and identify the required equipment and accessories.
Match received serial numbers and quantities against the order and asset records.
Inspect equipment, ports, packaging and accessories for visible damage or omissions.
Connect equipment and run standard startup, peripheral and hardware diagnostics.
Decide whether equipment is ready or requires correction before delivery.
Update the asset record and delivery request with readiness and intended recipient.
Prepare the equipment label and packing checklist.
Attach the label, pack accessories and stage equipment for delivery.

tasks.design: Join approved orders in the {PROCUREMENT} to asset and delivery records in the {HELPDESK}, using deterministic serial-number and quantity checks. Configure diagnostic utilities represented by {OTHER} to return structured results, then require a specialist's release decision. Generate labels and packing checklists from approved records while physical inspection and packing remain hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order, asset and diagnostic records were separate, and physical checks could not be replaced by paperwork automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured order exports, barcode capture and diagnostic results support ordinary integration. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and template work; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Unpacking, connecting, inspecting and packing remain physical. Missing serial numbers, unusual peripherals and unreliable diagnostics create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting physical defects and recognising a device that passes diagnostics but is unsuitable for the user.

ambition.what: A ready-equipment pool for urgent replacements.

tasks.altitude: The week has fewer record checks and more equipment preparation and exception handling. Within an agreed stock allocation, the specialist can prioritise ready replacements; purchasing authority does not change.

reach.task: Coordinate equipment collection and confirm the intended recipient.
reach.learn: Collection scheduling, recipient checks and clear custody records.

evidence.claim: Structured order matching, diagnostic checklists and label generation can use deterministic technology.
Physical inspection and equipment handling remain manual without additional specialised hardware.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Goods receipt already captures serial numbers, or existing barcode capture can supply them.
The OTHER slot means device-management and hardware-diagnostic utilities.
Supported diagnostics expose structured results; plugging in equipment remains human work.
Asset records are held in the service desk rather than an assumed spreadsheet.
Access estimates include GDPR review of recipient records and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Are received serial numbers captured reliably?
Which device and peripheral tests can run unattended?
Where are asset assignment and readiness recorded today?
Who authorises release and replacement-stock allocation?
Can existing printers and scanners use the generated labels?
research_questions: Which diagnostic failures reliably predict equipment rejection?
Can current configuration cover order matching before a connector is built?
Which physical checks prevent the most delivery rework?
new_work: Resolve unmatched serial numbers and order discrepancies.
Maintain equipment standards and diagnostic checklists.
Check failed or incomplete diagnostic runs.
Maintain label templates and connector mappings.
Review release exceptions and replacement-pool stock accuracy.
tasks.statement: Inspect equipment and read order sheets to prepare for delivery to users.

tasks.short: Adapt commercial software through supported configuration and small extensions.

steps.what: Clarify the requested behaviour and agree acceptance criteria.
Check documented configuration options, extension interfaces and support restrictions.
Configure the {OTHER} commercial application in a test environment.
Write necessary extensions in the {OTHER} development environment.

loop.input: Approved requirements, supported interfaces, relevant existing code and test fixtures.
loop.output: A small extension patch and proposed tests in an isolated development workspace.
loop.check: Run syntax, security and regression checks; specialist reviews the diff and interface compatibility.
loop.stop: At most two patch attempts per bounded change; failing checks or unsupported interfaces return work to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use configuration first. Where it cannot express the required behaviour, writing a new extension requires contextual code synthesis.

steps.what: Run regression checks using {OTHER} software testing tools.
Validate changed behaviour against real work examples.
Release accepted changes through the {OTHER} application administration console.
Update the change record and configuration history.

tasks.design: Use supported configuration in the {OTHER} commercial application before building extensions. For genuine gaps, a bounded coding loop drafts a patch in the {OTHER} development environment; deterministic checks produce evidence in {HELPDESK}, users accept behaviour, and the application owner approves release. Generate change records in {DOCS} from the release manifest.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small changes still require environment knowledge, testing and release coordination. Unsupported customisations create upgrade risk, while manual configuration is difficult to reproduce.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable configuration templates, test fixtures and release manifests reduce repeated work. Coding assistance can draft bounded extensions, but its benefit depends on the application and the specialist's review effort.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented interfaces, weak test coverage, licensing restrictions and upgrades can make extensions expensive. Passing automated checks does not prove that a change fits real work.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether a request merits customisation, recognises unsupported approaches and negotiates acceptable behaviour with users.

ambition.what: A supported configuration clinic for small customer service teams.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time repeating configuration and change paperwork, and more time shaping requirements and reviewing behaviour. They can select approved configuration patterns within a defined remit; release authority remains with the application owner.

reach.task: Describe repetitive case-handling steps and validate a proposed configuration change.
reach.learn: Learn service workflows, acceptance-example writing and how configuration affects frontline handling.

reach.task: Improve reusable response templates and document-routing rules.
reach.learn: Learn document controls, exception routing and accessible template design.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review with expected human oversight, supporting bounded patch drafting.
Developer field trials reported increased completed tasks with coding assistance; this does not establish a tenfold build-speed gain.
A controlled study found experienced developers slower with early assistance tools, showing that review and context costs can outweigh gains.
Supported configuration, reproducible tests and controlled releases are feasible without autonomous production access.

assumptions: Shares describe a mixed workload of configuration changes and small extensions; configuration-only requests skip extension work.
The target application exposes supported configuration or extension interfaces.
Build ranges cover a reusable path for one application and one small pilot change.
The coding loop has isolated development access and no production credentials.
Test data is synthetic or minimised under GDPR.
National consultation requirements are assessed if changes affect working methods or employee monitoring; elapsed approval time may exceed the effort range.
unknowns: Which application and supported extension mechanisms are involved?
Are test environments, rollback facilities and representative fixtures available?
Who owns acceptance and release decisions?
What do support terms and licences permit?
Which personal data would development and testing expose?
What access and employee consultation are required?
research_questions: Which requested behaviours can be met through supported configuration before any extension is considered?
Which regression checks detect the application's most consequential failure modes?
new_work: Review generated patches and configuration differences.
Maintain regression fixtures and supported configuration patterns.
Handle failed checks and unsupported requests.
Retest extensions after application upgrades.
Maintain release permissions, rollback procedures and generated change records.
tasks.statement: Modify and customize commercial programs for internal needs.

tasks.short: Assess office automation options through workflow observation, space assessment and cost comparison.

steps.what: Agree the study question, constraints and success criteria.
Observe staff performing the workflow and discuss exceptions.
Survey equipment locations, space constraints and accessibility needs.
Collect workload, delay and incident figures from available records.
Compare implementation costs, running costs and benefit scenarios.
Write feasible options with dependencies, risks and space implications.

loop.input: Observed workflow, measured constraints, calculated costs and specialist-selected options.
loop.output: An options paper separating evidence, assumptions, dependencies and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link factual claims to supplied records; copy financial results from calculated fields; specialist reviews feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unsupported claims remain marked unknown and return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but describing trade-offs across varied observations requires prose synthesis.

steps.what: Validate options with affected staff and the process owner.
Approve the study recommendation or request further evidence.

tasks.design: A reusable study generator on {DATA_PLATFORM} imports approved records from {HELPDESK} and {PROJECT}, then calculates cost scenarios from explicit assumptions. A bounded loop drafts an options paper in {DOCS}; staff validate operational effects and the operations manager approves the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Studies are infrequent and differ in scope. Baselines, quotes and observations arrive in different formats, making a reusable process costly to assemble.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable import mappings, calculation templates and document generation reduce repeated assembly work. A bounded loop can organise free-text observations without choosing the investment.
tasks.still_hard: Observed time savings may not become cash savings. Physical constraints, accessibility, organisational resistance and incomplete workload records require fieldwork and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist notices workarounds, challenges optimistic assumptions and explains trade-offs to affected people.

ambition.what: A fixed-scope feasibility review for small reception and administrative teams.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling tables and more time observing work and testing assumptions. They can recommend a pilot within an agreed study remit; investment approval remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Assess a proposed change to appointment handling or document processing.
reach.learn: Learn workload sampling, capacity planning and the difference between released time and cash savings.

evidence.claim: Explicit cost formulas, scenario tables and templated reports can automate study assembly without automating investment judgement.
A field study reported more completed developer tasks with coding assistance; this does not establish feasibility-study savings.
GDPR applies to identifiable workflow observations; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed monitoring.

assumptions: Shares describe a small study that includes both workflow and space assessment.
Build ranges cover reusable tooling for a limited set of record formats, not the fieldwork for every study.
The initial baseline uses aggregate workload figures rather than individual productivity scores.
Consent and access effort includes consultation under national rules where required; elapsed approval time may be longer.
The study decision does not authorise purchasing or production deployment.
unknowns: Which workload records exist and what do their timestamps mean?
Are supplier quotes and internal cost rates available?
Who owns the process and approves the recommendation?
What consultation is required for observation or changes to working methods?
Which floor plans and accessibility constraints are current?
research_questions: Which sampling method gives a useful baseline without collecting unnecessary employee-level data?
new_work: Maintain import mappings and cost assumptions.
Check draft claims against observations and calculations.
Investigate missing or inconsistent baseline records.
Compare pilot outcomes with the original benefit assumptions.
Refresh access, retention and consultation arrangements when study scope changes.
tasks.statement: Conduct office automation feasibility studies, including workflow analysis, space design, or cost comparison analysis.

tasks.short: Select and supervise staff delivering technical projects, troubleshooting and installations.

steps.what: Agree project scope, required skills and staffing needs.
Prepare the role brief and staffing request.
Review candidate evidence against agreed role requirements.
Interview candidates and assess technical and collaborative skills.
Approve the appointment recommendation and employment terms.
Assign project work, responsibilities and escalation paths.
Coach workers, resolve blockers and direct technical problem-solving.
Check progress, dependencies and unresolved installation issues.
Accept completed work against agreed technical criteria.

tasks.design: Configure role templates and approval routing around {ATS}, and reusable assignment checklists and progress views in {PROJECT}. Link project issues to {HELPDESK} and acceptance evidence in {DOCS}; people select candidates, coach workers, approve assignments and accept completed work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision mixes relationships, staffing judgement and administration, so it was treated as one indivisible activity. Progress evidence is often split between project records and incident records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, task dependencies and dashboard configuration can remove repeated coordination work. Small deterministic connectors can join records without introducing automated employee assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Fair hiring, conflict resolution, coaching and judging readiness remain personal responsibilities. Reliable status data requires workers to record meaningful progress.
tasks.human_edge: The lead recognises developing capability, handles disagreement and balances delivery pressure with safe, sustainable work.

ambition.what: Offer supervised technical project placements to customer service staff.

tasks.altitude: The lead spends less time assembling updates and more time coaching and unblocking work. Within an agreed project remit, they can allocate bounded learning assignments; hiring and production-change rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Allocate work and coach staff during a service-process change.
reach.learn: Learn structured coaching, workload balancing and how to assess learning assignments fairly.

reach.task: Triage simple technical enquiries during a supervised placement.
reach.learn: Learn safe diagnostic scripts, escalation limits and clear incident recording.

evidence.claim: Configured task templates, dependencies and progress views can reduce administrative coordination while supervision stays human.
Recruitment and worker-management AI can fall within EU AI Act Annex III; this design excludes automated candidate ranking and worker scoring.
GDPR and applicable national employment and consultation rules affect candidate data and employee monitoring.

assumptions: This supplemental task is performed by a senior specialist with delegated team-lead duties.
Shares represent a combined staffing and project-supervision cycle; hiring is intermittent.
The recruiter handles offer issue and onboarding through the wider hiring workflow.
Assignment suggestions use approved task templates and availability, without inferring employee performance.
Build ranges cover one team and existing recruitment and project processes.
Consultation effort is conditional on national rules and changes to employee monitoring; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: What hiring, assignment and acceptance authority does the specialist hold?
How often does this role participate in recruitment?
Are availability and project status records current?
Can project and incident records be linked with appropriate access?
What employee consultation is required for new progress views?
research_questions: Which team-level progress indicators reveal delivery blockers without becoming individual productivity scores?
new_work: Maintain role templates, assignment checklists and escalation paths.
Review proposed assignments before they reach workers.
Correct stale availability and progress records.
Review access to candidate and employee information.
Check that dashboards remain focused on work dependencies rather than worker rankings.
tasks.statement: Hire, supervise, and direct workers engaged in special project work, problem-solving, monitoring, and installation of data communication equipment and software.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward service impact, difficult diagnosis and helping users complete their work. Delegated rights can expand to investigation priorities and knowledge improvement proposals; access, purchasing and disruptive change approvals remain explicitly assigned.
reach: First-line support supervisor: connect incident patterns to queue coverage and coaching.
Customer service representative: improve clarification, explanation and escalation.
Correspondence clerk: turn approved technical information into clear written instructions.
skills_to_grow: Configure request workflows, endpoint profiles and knowledge search.
Understand API permissions, identifiers and integration failures.
Evaluate technical evidence and version-specific guidance.
Test repair procedures and recovery checks.
Write accessible instructions and conduct effective user conversations.
Apply data minimisation and recognise when national consultation rules matter.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A support specialist who uses reliable service evidence to propose prevention work, offers individual setup clinics and extends approved guidance beyond staffed hours.

role_batches.altitude: The specialist spends less time deploying standard packages, watching routine checks, and copying records. More time goes to difficult faults, user conversations, and prevention; rollout-pause authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Customer service representative: design clear first-contact checks and handovers.
Office support supervisor: turn recurring support demand into prioritised service changes.
Correspondence clerk: turn verified fixes into understandable user instructions.
skills_to_grow: Diagnostic scripting and explicit pass, fail, and unknown criteria.
Endpoint deployment, rollback, and event integration.
Requirements facilitation and acceptance criteria.
Evidence review, privacy-aware documentation, and fault-pattern analysis.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a small service-improvement practice: combine recurring-fault evidence, readiness checks, and evening-shift requirements clinics to propose targeted changes for service-owner approval.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from assembling records and paperwork toward difficult faults, representative testing and practical coaching. Proposed delegation covers review priorities, lesson topics and replacement allocation within agreed limits; spending and broader policy decisions stay with their existing approvers.
reach: Customer service representatives: service recovery and clear technical explanations.
First-line supervisors of office and administrative support workers: workflow observation and change adoption.
Receptionists and information clerks: equipment collection and custody coordination.
skills_to_grow: Configure service and learning workflows.
Define reusable records, decision rules and exception paths.
Validate source-linked summaries and extracted specifications.
Design representative technical and usability tests.
Teach through practice and accessible instructions.
Apply GDPR data minimisation and recognise consultation requirements under national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A support improvement specialist who turns recurring faults into tested upgrade proposals, accessible training and a ready-equipment replacement service, while keeping consequential technical and spending decisions accountable.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from collecting information and maintaining coordination records toward technical judgement, user coaching and controlled service improvement. Additional decision rights should be explicit: selecting learning topics, proposing bounded pilots and choosing approved configuration patterns within an agreed remit.
reach: Help receptionists resolve common workstation and meeting-room problems.
Help administrative supervisors assess workflow changes and benefit assumptions.
Coach customer service staff through supervised technical triage placements.
Help correspondence clerks improve response templates and routing rules.
skills_to_grow: Requirements discovery and acceptance-example writing.
Supported configuration and interface design.
Deterministic testing, release evidence and rollback.
Cost modelling and workload sampling.
Source evaluation and technical teaching.
Coaching, fair selection and workload allocation.
GDPR data minimisation and consultation under national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a technical service improvement lead who runs small feasibility reviews, teaches frontline troubleshooting and delivers supported configuration changes with clear evidence. People retain hiring, investment and release decisions; reusable tools make preparation and follow-through cheaper.
